question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mint city and its role in British India's monetization of the economy]
options: Calcutta Mint — Established 1829; became the primary mint producing Company rupees for Bengal and eastern India
Bombay Mint — Struck silver rupees and later became active in gold sovereign production for western India
Madras Mint — Produced the Madras fanam and later Company coinage for southern Presidency transactions
Lahore Mint — Established by the British in 1820 to monetize Punjab's predominantly barter economy
wrong_fact: The British did NOT establish a mint in Lahore in 1820. Punjab was under Sikh rule (Ranjit Singh's empire) until 1849. The British acquired Punjab only after the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1849), so a British-run Lahore Mint in 1820 is anachronistic and false.
explanation: Calcutta and Bombay Mints were key British India coinage centres. Madras did have its own coinage tradition. However, Lahore was under Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire until 1849 — the British could not have established a mint there in 1820. After annexation of Punjab in 1849, the Lahore Mint did come under British control, but not as an 1820 establishment.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Region/community and the impact of monetization/cash-revenue demand on it]
options: Deccan ryots — Forced into money-lender debt (sahukars) as Ryotwari cash demands replaced barter in kind
Punjab peasants — Post-1849 annexation, cash revenue demands accelerated alienation of land to urban moneylenders
Bengal zamindars — Permanent Settlement's fixed cash demand caused sub-infeudation and rack-renting of tenants
Rajputana tribal communities — Monetization had negligible effect as the princely states maintained a fully self-sufficient grain-barter system untouched by British revenue law
wrong_fact: Rajputana's tribal communities were NOT fully insulated from monetization. Even in princely states, British paramountcy, trade penetration, and the broader monetized economy affected revenue systems and exchange. Claiming these areas were 'untouched by British revenue law' and maintained a 'fully self-sufficient barter system' is an overstatement and factually incorrect.
explanation: Deccan ryot indebtedness to moneylenders (leading to the Deccan Riots of 1875) is well-documented. Punjab land alienation due to cash demands led to the Punjab Land Alienation Act 1900. Bengal zamindars used sub-infeudation to pass on Permanent Settlement pressures to tenants. Rajputana princely states had their own revenue systems but were not hermetically sealed from British economic influence or monetization trends.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Banking/financial institution established during colonial monetization and its operational geography]
options: Bank of Bengal (1806) — Calcutta; first presidency bank, extended credit for colonial trade and revenue collection
Bank of Bombay (1840) — Bombay; facilitated monetization of cotton trade and later merged into Imperial Bank
Bank of Madras (1843) — Madras; supported southern Presidency trade including coffee and indigo financing
Allahabad Bank (1865) — Established in Allahabad as the first entirely Indian-owned scheduled bank to support NWP monetization
wrong_fact: Allahabad Bank (1865) was NOT the first entirely Indian-owned scheduled bank. It was founded by a group of Europeans in Allahabad. Punjab National Bank (1894, Lahore) is often cited as among the first Indian-owned banks. Allahabad Bank had European founders and was not a purely Indian enterprise.
explanation: The three Presidency Banks — Bank of Bengal (1806), Bank of Bombay (1840), Bank of Madras (1843) — are correctly placed geographically and later merged to form the Imperial Bank of India (1921). Allahabad Bank was established in 1865 in Allahabad but by European promoters, not as an Indian-owned institution — making that description incorrect.
